physicalNotes: Radius 0.25961326 Jupiter radii from Mann et al. 2023 (2023AJ....165..217M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..217M/abstract): 18,560.3 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. No mass is measured: Mann et al. 2023 (2023AJ....165..217M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..217M/abstract) gives only an upper limit of 3.5 Jupiter masses, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Mann et al. 2023 (2023AJ....165..217M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MANN_ET_AL__2023): P 91.68278 d
sources.shape: Mann et al. 2023 (2023AJ....165..217M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MANN_ET_AL__2023): a/R* 83.7; Mann et al. 2023 (2023AJ....165..217M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MANN_ET_AL__2023): inclination 89.75 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Mann et al. 2023 (2023AJ....165..217M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MANN_ET_AL__2023): transit mid-time 2458404.1791 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 14 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
